edges.effect_quant: Mostly mechanistic and preclinical work suggest the direction is more reliable than any single pooled magnitude.
edges.mechanism: EPA and DHA lower hepatic VLDL production, shift membrane lipid signaling, and can modestly dampen inflammatory eicosanoid tone. Those mechanisms matter most for Chronic systemic inflammation when baseline triglycerides are high or the outcome is tightly linked to cardiometabolic inflammation.
edges.summary: Omega-3 in adults with high triglycerides appears tied to lower chronic systemic inflammation in adults with elevated triglycerides mainly through mostly mechanistic and preclinical work. The likely magnitude is modest, which is why the edge is framed conservatively rather than as a headline-level breakthrough.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.
